content:
lina: quick sync on the canary that ejected bursty tenants. want a compact decision record so we don’t repeat this.

omar: short version: blended scoring made transient spikes look like sustained abuse. we should require orthogonal signals before hard eject.

vik: proposal: two-stage policy. short-window detects spikes -> soft-shed (concurrency cap). long-window detects sustained share -> fairness action. hard eject only if short && long && host_health_bad.

hazel: add host_health_bad = tail_latency_p99 > 1s OR queue_depth > 75%. reserved customers skip hard path and trigger SLA alert.

ops-bot: canary deployed: v1.2.7 -> region-us-west :rocket:

lina: minimal config snippet for RFC appendix:
```json
{
  "short_window_s": "30",
  "short_metric": "instant_share",
  "short_thresh": "0.85",
  "soft_action": "concurrency_cap_50pct",
  "long_window_s": "3600",
  "long_metric": "p95_share",
  "long_thresh": "0.65",
  "hard_eject_if": "short && long && host_health",
  "enable_hard_eject": "false # feature flag",
  "reserved_tiers": "bypass_hard_alert_only"
}
```

omar: telemetry checklist to add before enabling flag: per-tenant short_hits, probation_entries, hard_ejects_total; per-host p99_latency and queue_depth. dashboard + alert thresholds.

vik: ops playbook sketch: page on hard_eject_rate>0.3%/min, run `tenant-inspect`, if reserved -> notify account, otherwise consider rollback `rlsctl eject --undo`.

lina: next steps: eng-platform updates RFC + config; eng-sre owns runbook and flag rollout plan. i'll PR the RFC later today.

hazel: agree. keep feature flag off by default and gate by region until we validate recovery behavior. :thumbsup:
